en.heading: 25 June: Filipino seafarers and the Manila maritime agreement
en.origin: The Day of the Filipino Seafarer recognizes workers who navigate commercial shipping routes and contribute to international transport, family livelihoods and the Philippine economy. en.heading: 24–30 August: National Coconut Week and agricultural livelihoods
en.origin: National Coconut Week highlights the role of coconut farms and processing in Philippine rural livelihoods, including growers, labourers, traders and the industries using coconut products. President Corazon Aquino issued Proclamation No. 142 on 19 August 1987, declaring the period 24–30 August 1987 and every year thereafter National Coconut Week under the Philippine Coconut Authority. The original document says August is a peak coconut season and invites the whole industry, from growers to policy-makers, to participate. Its seven-day August period is not a general international coconut holiday.

en.heading: 4 July: Republic Day and the transfer of Independence Day to June
en.origin: The historical 4 July anniversary recalls the formal recognition of Philippine independence from the United States on 4 July 1946, after the Second World War. It must be distinguished from the 12 June 1898 declaration. Republic Act No. 4166, approved on 4 August 1964, moved the national Independence Day observance to 12 June and named 4 July Philippine Republic Day, listing it then among legal holidays. Executive Order No. 292, the 1987 Administrative Code, later listed national regular holidays without 4 July. A historical Republic Day entry therefore cannot be labeled a currently recurring regular non-working holiday on the basis of the 1964 law alone.

La Legge della Repubblica n. 4166, approvata il 4 agosto 1964, spostò la Giornata dell'indipendenza al 12 giugno e chiamò il 4 luglio Philippine Republic Day, allora nell'elenco delle festività legali. L'Ordine esecutivo n. 292, Codice amministrativo del 1987, elencò le festività regolari senza il 4 luglio. La scheda storica non può definirlo oggi un giorno non lavorativo ordinario basandosi solo sulla legge del 1964.

en.heading: 2 April: Araw ni Balagtas honours a poet and the Filipino language
en.origin: Araw ni Balagtas commemorates Francisco Balagtas Baltazar, a major poet born on 2 April 1788 and remembered for the literary work Florante at Laura. The specific national day honours his literary legacy, not a generic biography list. Proclamation No. 1249 of 1 April 1974 established the annual celebration on 2 April and described a special holiday in the province of Bulacan. The exact present-day provincial non-working status requires checking the annual calendar. President Corazon Aquino's Proclamation No. 5 of 1 April 1986 again called for an annual Araw ni Balagtas. The 1986 reiteration should not erase the earlier 1974 legal declaration or be mistaken for its first origin.
